paras: The killing of Henry Green was the fatal shooting of a Black man by Deputy Sheriff T. G. Martin at Kyle, Texas, on Sunday, July 30, 1882, while Martin was trying to arrest him on a warrant. Green died the next day in the jail at San Marcos, and a coroner's jury found that he died of a shot fired by Martin, who was bound over to the district court.

Justice Lynch had issued a warrant charging Green, whom the San Marcos Free Press called "a negro," with assault with attempt to kill Thos. Shea, a section boss at Kyle. Martin, a deputy sheriff from Kyle, was seeking to serve that warrant.

Martin shot Green on Sunday, July 30. According to the Free Press, "it is claimed" that Green resisted arrest, but he was shot while running. Because no place could be found for him at Kyle, the wounded man was brought to San Marcos and put in the upper room of the jail, where the paper said he was "properly cared for." He died there on Monday, July 31.

An inquest was held before Squire Grooms, and the jury returned a verdict of death from a shot fired by T. G. Martin on July 30, 1882. Martin was bound over in the sum of $1,000 to answer at the next term of the district court. In the same issue, a one-line local item reported that Martin had resigned his position as deputy sheriff. No report of an indictment or trial was found in the coverage.

The only known report is a short local item in the San Marcos Free Press of August 3, 1882, headed "Another Killing at Kyle." The paper gave the claim of resistance as a claim and set against it that Green was shot while running, without further comment. It said it lacked space to print the inquest proceedings in full and gave only the substance as furnished by Squire Grooms. Martin's resignation appeared separately among advertisements and local notes in the paper's "Home News" column, with no link drawn to the shooting.

reader.title: Killing of Henry Green
bases: A deputy sheriff acting alone shot Green while trying to serve an arrest warrant on him; no crowd or posse is reported (A1).
Only the San Marcos Free Press reported the shooting, in one article, with a related brief in the same issue (A1, A3).
